issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s use of a room in an otherwise residential building as a tailoring shop does not, by itself, make the building non-residential.
material_facts: The building was built for residential purposes and was primarily used as a residence.
The tenant occupied two rooms, used one for living purposes, and ran a tailoring shop in the other.
The landlord occupied the remaining part of the building for residential purposes.
issues.conclusion: The tailoring shop did not convert the otherwise residential building into a non-residential building.
issues.legal_principle: For purposes of section 21(1), Explanation (iv), of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, a building otherwise residential in character does not cease to be residential merely because a tenant conducts a tailoring business in one room. The Court relied on no earlier cases for this holding.

predicates.residential_tenancy_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant from a building on personal-requirement grounds.
predicates.building_primarily_used_as_residence: The building was built for residential purposes and was primarily used as a residence.
predicates.tenant_runs_business_in_room: The tenant conducted a business in one room of the building.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding concerns a building built and primarily used as a residence, the tenant’s business use of one room does not change its residential character.

issues.legal_issue: When a residential building is partly occupied by the landlord for residential purposes and the remaining part is occupied by the tenant, bona fide requirement is conclusively presumed.
material_facts: The building was residential in character.
The landlord occupied part of the building for residential purposes, and the tenant occupied the remaining part.
The landlord sought vacant possession so that the family could live together in the building.
issues.conclusion: The statutory conditions for the conclusive and irrebuttable presumption of bona fide requirement were met, and the landlord did not need to establish any further requirement.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(1), Explanation (iv), of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, provides a conclusive and irrebuttable presumption of bona fide requirement where the building is residential, the landlord occupies part of it for residential purposes, and the tenant occupies another part. No earlier cases were relied upon.

rule.if: residential_tenancy_eviction_proceeding and building_is_residential and landlord_occupies_part_for_residence and tenant_occupies_other_part

predicates.residential_tenancy_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant from a building on personal-requirement grounds.
predicates.building_is_residential: The building was residential in character.
predicates.landlord_occupies_part_for_residence: The landlord occupied part of the building for residential purposes.
predicates.tenant_occupies_other_part: The tenant occupied another part of the same building.

issues.definition: In a residential tenancy eviction proceeding, the landlord’s residential occupation of part of a residential building and the tenant’s occupation of another part result in the landlord’s bona fide requirement being conclusively established.
